Her element, carried in her design: moscovium: a synthetic superheavy element first made in 2003 at a science town on the upper reaches of a great northern river, by firing calcium ions at an americium target in a joint effort with a laboratory across the ocean, and named for the snowbound region around that town and its red-walled capital; each atom lives less than a second before decaying into nihonium, and it was at the end of its decay chains that nihonium was first glimpsed; it sits below nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony and bismuth and is predicted to be a heavy, soft metal.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Brick-crimson knight plate with big rounded pauldrons and layered plates below the waist, every edge rimed with frost-white crystal trim, small golden dome-shaped caps on the shoulders and knees, a deep pine-green inner suit, a slender crown-like head ornament with a tiny golden dome instead of a helmet, a warm ember-gold core at the chest; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.

Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a red fortress city in endless snow: vast walls clad in red armour plates with star-tipped spires, warm golden-domed greenhouses sheltered inside the walls, and a deep accelerator stronghold firing its beam through the blizzard.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Mc) and atomic number (115) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
